title.narrative: Emergency Assistance for Reconstruction and Recovery of Marawi

description.narrative: The emergency assistance (ERRM) is structured to provide the GoP with immediate and flexible financing to implement programs, projects and activities included in the Bangon Marawi Comprehensive Rehabilitation and Recovery Program.

Progress Toward Outcome: The COVID-19 crisis exacerbated the situation of the displaced families struggle to get back to normalcy after the siege.
Construction of new public infrastructures in MAAs of Marawi City started in December 2019. Priority goes to school buildings with 200 classrooms, 24 barangay halls with health center and madrasa, 50-bed capacity hospital, and the Grand Padian market. The government earmarked additional PhP 3.5 billion for the reconstruction efforts from the 2020 national budget.
For Output 2: As of 30 September 2024, there are 4 ongoing civil works contracts, 1 is ongoing procurement with bid submission deadline date of 5 November 2024 (CP1C) while 2 are for procurement (CP02 and CP4B/CP03). Estimated cumulative progress for civil works is 100% for CP1A and CP1B, 46.36% for CP05 and 28.68% for CP4A.
Feasibility Studies and detailed engineering design progress is 100.00%.
For CP02 Construction of Malabang Viaduct (the largest contract package under the project), ADB reviewed the draft bidding document and shared the comments with DPWH on 16 July 2024 for their consideration and necessary action. ADB issued no objection to the BD on 20 September 2024. The IEE was disclosed on 5 June 2024 while the RP in August 2024. CP02 is for tender in October 2024.
The recruitment for the External Monitoring Agent for REMDP/RP was completed in August 2024 and the consultant mobilized the following month.
ADB received the request for a 42-month loan validity extension from the Department of Finance on 28 June 2024. ADB project team has since been working on the Board Paper seeking Board approval for a waiver to the maximum implementation period limit for an emergency assistance loan.
For Output 3, the grant was financially closed on 4 September 2024.
For Output 4, the grant was financially closed on 30 April 2024.

Status of Implementation Progress: Grant closing date was extended to 31 December 2023. The procurement of mobile health units was cancelled in November 2020 due to significant issues to procure the units, including significant time- and cost overruns. The goods were already delivered to the health facilities. Construction of Marawi CHU and Lumbayanague RHU are already completed as of 30 June 2023. They are both now operational.
The patient transport and monitoring vehicles and ambulances have been delivered to the recipient LGUs. DOH agreed to cancel the procurement of mobile health clinics, following several failures of bidding due to difficulty in sourcing out suppliers and likely shortage of funds arising from an expected increase in cost for the construction of health units and procurement of medical equipment. Contracts for goods have also been awarded as of 31 December 2021. The goods were already delivered to the health facilities. Construction of Marawi CHU and Lumbayanague RHU are already completed as of 30 June 2023. They are both now operational.
Grant closing date was extended to 31 December 2023.
Significant delays by COVID 19 impacts. Contract award for CW-02 WS (DC) in August 2020, civil works started in December 2020. CW-01 WS was awarded in May 2021. The contracts are expected for completion by November 2023.
Funds under the Output will be insufficient to cover full pipe replacement in the 19 Barangays, ADB and LWUA agreed to implement the revised targets with the current available funds as far as possible (12 barangays) (>15.4km).
A total of 15,156.9 m of pipelines will be replaced (8,227.9 m for CW-01 WS and 6,929 m for CW-02 WS) including additional lengths for cross pipes.
Contract CW-01 WS: As of 30-Nov-2023, LWUA reported accomplishment of 100%.
Contract CW-02 WS: As of 30-Nov-2023, LWUA reported accomplishment of 100%.
As of 27 April 2020, L3768-PHI has been fully disbursed ($300 million). Besides the programs, projects, and activities under the Bangon Marawi Comprehensice Recovery and Rehabilitation Program (BMCRRP), the quick-disbursing component of ERRM supported recurrent expenditures and maintenance and other operating expenses for schools in Marawi City and Lanao del Sur, as well as the Marawi State University.
As of 30 September 2024, there are 4 ongoing civil works contracts, 1 is ongoing procurement with bid submission deadline date of 5 November 2024 (CP1C) while 2 are for procurement (CP02 and CP4B/CP03). Estimated cumulative progress for civil works is 100% for CP1A and CP1B, 46.36% for CP05 and 28.68% for CP4A.
The draft BD for the combined CP4B and CP03 is under ADB review. Safeguards documents are still under review for CP03.
Feasibility Studies and detailed engineering design progress is 100.00%.
For CP02 Construction of Malabang Viaduct (the largest contract package under the project), ADB reviewed the draft bidding document and shared the comments with DPWH on 16 July 2024 for their consideration and necessary action. ADB issued no objection to the BD on 20 September 2024. The IEE was disclosed on 5 June 2024 while the RP in August 2024. CP02 is for tender in October 2024.
The draft BD for the combined CP4B and CP03 is under ADB review. Safeguards documents for CP03 were prepared and are still under review.
The recruitment for the External Monitoring Agent for REMDP/RP was completed in August 2024 and the consultant mobilized the following month.
As of July 2022, overall component 2 has 1,939 enrolled beneficiaries, (553) 29% male, (1,366) 71% female and 420 ( 21% ) youth composed of Youth Male 164 and Youth Female 256. The 1,200 sustainable livelihoods beneficiaries target is completed exceeding 739 (62%) exceed achievement.
For the reporting period, 1,674 /1,939 beneficiaries improved their business skills through a series of trainings (eg. entrepreneurial orientations, production Capacity, Product Costing, Product Marketing, Product Selling, Packaging and Marketing Strategy). 86% of livelihood program beneficiaries including IPs/Ems with enhanced business skills.
Construction of the bagsakan facility has been completed as of September 2022.
As of 31 December 2022, 200 classrooms were provided with school furniture. A total of 150 units of foot operated hand washing kiosk was delivered to benefit 69 schools. As much as possible these schools received the school furniture to improve quality learning environment.
As of July 2022, the project's accomplishment is 100% (with 7% above reach accomplishment) of the target 2,400. 2,573 beneficiaries who completed the program are women (50%) and youth (24%) [male- 347 (57%), female- 266 (43%)]. This excludes the days of work reserved by SCP to contribute to landscaping of the facilities to be constructed under components 2 and 3 for community building.
Construction of the school building completed as of 31 December 2022.
As of March 2022, in terms of procurement, SCP delivered all 13 multicopiers to schools.
SCP has completed product enhancement and business skills trainings for all beneficiaries in the individual and group livelihoods programs. Online marketing platforms and digital solutions were launched to minimize the isolating impact COVID-19 has had on the supply chain.
Training was conducted after development MHPSS modules for Bangsamoro learners. MHPSS training of trainers was conducted in September 2022.
Team of professionals for the development of MHPSS for Muslim Learners were engaged. MHPSS materials developed included peace, conflict-sensitive and gender-sensitive messages.
The project has engaged three youth engagement platforms namely, the Youth Leadership and Peace Summit, the Ranaw Youth Parliament and the Socially Excluded Youth. This covers the participation of youth in the executive and legislative arm in governance.
101 (Male -59, F, 42) youth participated in Youth Leadership Summit, female youth consisted of 42% of the total participants on this activity. The youth participants are from municipalities of Mulondo, Taraka Tamparan, Saguiaran, Butig, Lumba Bayabao, Pagayawan, Marantao, Marawi City and Maguing as part of efforts for Youth Peace Education for protection against recruitment to violent extremism in partnership with Armed Forces of the Philippines and UNDP.
52 (26 (50%) male, 26 (50%) female) youth participated in the Ranaw Youth Peace and Development training.
50 (20 (40%) male, 30 (60%) female) socially excluded youth participated in the Peacetival activities.
52 youth (23 male, 29 female) from municipalities of LDS participated in the 2nd Youth Leadership Summit conducted last July 26-30, 2021 in Marawi City, LDS supported by the project with focused areas on leadership skills formation and Peace Education. These youth will be engaged in the multi -stakeholder network for peace action.
Conflict sensitive and peacebuilding workshop conducted on May 24-26 to consolidate the peace action plan. A peacebuilding network strengthening was also conducted with the Education Workers Network of MBHTE to strengthen Peace Coalition with the Education Sector on June 20-22.
20 young leaders completed the Ranaw Young Leaders' Academy (RYLA) course. The module is finalized and will be the benchmark training course for young leaders for the province.
